classification.difficultyReason: Parts progress from direct parallel-line relationships to configurations requiring several angle transfers and a straight-angle calculation.

content.prompt: Using only properties of parallel lines, find (with reasons) the unknown angle $\theta$ in each of the following diagrams:

spec.description: Descending transversal crossing two horizontal parallel lines. The scan retains the upper parallel marker but loses the upper horizontal stroke; the native reconstruction restores that stroke.
spec.mathematics: The two labelled upper-left sectors are corresponding angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 110 degrees and unknown theta are visible.

teachingContext.methodNote: Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal.
teachingContext.mappingNote: The given and unknown occupy the same relative position at the two intersections.

spec.description: Ascending transversal crossing horizontal parallel lines. Both printed theta labels are retained in vertically opposite upper-intersection sectors. The missing upper horizontal stroke is restored.
spec.mathematics: Each theta is supplementary to the corresponding 85-degree sector; the two theta sectors are vertically opposite.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 85 degrees and both printed theta labels only.

answer.worked:
The upper-right angle at the upper intersection is $85^{\circ}$ (corresponding angles).
$$\theta=180^{\circ}-85^{\circ}=95^{\circ}$$
Angles on a straight line are supplementary. The second $\theta$ has the same value because vertically opposite angles are equal.

teachingContext.methodNote: Transfer the given angle by corresponding angles, then use supplementary adjacent angles.
teachingContext.mappingNote: Both printed theta labels occupy vertically opposite sectors and therefore denote the same unknown.

spec.description: Two steep parallel lines with upward markers crossed by a descending transversal; the labelled interior sectors lie on the same side of the transversal.

answer.worked:
$$\theta=180^{\circ}-130^{\circ}=50^{\circ}$$
Co-interior angles on parallel lines are supplementary.

teachingContext.mappingNote: The two marked sectors are interior to the parallel lines and on the same side of the transversal.

spec.description: Two steep parallel lines crossed by an ascending transversal. Theta is the acute sector above the transversal at the left intersection; 135 degrees is the adjacent obtuse sector at the right intersection.
spec.mathematics: Corresponding acute sectors are equal; the right acute sector is supplementary to 135 degrees.

answer.worked:
The angle above the transversal and to the right of the right parallel line is $180^{\circ}-135^{\circ}=45^{\circ}$ (angles on a straight line).
$$\theta=45^{\circ}$$
Corresponding angles are equal.

teachingContext.methodNote: Use a straight-angle calculation followed by corresponding angles.
teachingContext.mappingNote: The given is adjacent to the sector corresponding to theta.

spec.description: Slanted segment joining two rightward horizontal parallel rays. The upper horizontal stroke is absent in the scan and is restored from the surviving parallel marker.
spec.mathematics: Theta and 62 degrees are co-interior angles.

answer.worked:
$$\theta=180^{\circ}-62^{\circ}=118^{\circ}$$
Co-interior angles on parallel lines are supplementary.

teachingContext.mappingNote: The labels are between the horizontal parallels on the same side of the slanted segment.

spec.description: Descending transversal crossing horizontal parallel lines. Theta is below the upper line on the left and 123 degrees above the lower line on the right. The missing upper horizontal stroke is restored.
spec.mathematics: The labelled sectors are alternate interior angles.

answer.worked:
$$\theta=123^{\circ}$$
Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal.

teachingContext.mappingNote: The marked sectors lie between the horizontal parallels on opposite sides of the transversal.

spec.description: Parallelogram with one marker on each horizontal side and two markers on each slanted side; bottom side extends right.
spec.mathematics: The lower-left acute angle is supplementary to 125 degrees, and theta is its corresponding angle across the slanted parallels.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 125 degrees and exterior theta only.

answer.short:
$55^{\circ}$

Use supplementary co-interior angles, then corresponding angles.
answer.worked:
The lower-left interior angle is $180^{\circ}-125^{\circ}=55^{\circ}$ (co-interior angles on the horizontal parallel lines).
$$\theta=55^{\circ}$$
Corresponding angles on the slanted parallel lines are equal.

teachingContext.methodNote: Combine co-interior and corresponding angle properties, as in the compound parallel configurations on page 6.
teachingContext.mappingNote: Two distinct pairs of parallel sides are marked, and theta is an exterior angle.

spec.description: Inverted triangle between a horizontal top side and a parallel horizontal line through the bottom vertex.
spec.mathematics: Transfer 62 and 33 degrees to the bottom horizontal line by alternate angles; the three adjacent angles there sum to 180 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 62 and 33 degrees and interior theta only.

answer.short:
$85^{\circ}$

Transfer both given angles to the lower parallel line, then use a straight angle.
answer.worked:
The angles beside $\theta$ on the lower line are $62^{\circ}$ and $33^{\circ}$ (alternate angles).
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^{\circ}-62^{\circ}-33^{\circ}\\\theta&=85^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.

teachingContext.methodNote: Use the parallel-line proof approach of page 6 Example 1(b), transferring angles before applying a straight angle.
teachingContext.mappingNote: The instruction restricts the solution to parallel-line properties, so no triangle-angle-sum shortcut is used.

spec.description: Two slanted lines cross above a horizontal triangle base and continue upwards. A horizontal parallel line passes through their intersection.
spec.mathematics: The angle between the upper-left ray and the left horizontal ray is 50 degrees by corresponding angles; this angle, theta and 30 degrees form a straight angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 30 and 50 degrees and upper theta only.

answer.short:
$100^{\circ}$

Transfer $50^{\circ}$ to the upper line, then subtract both adjacent angles from $180^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
The angle between the upper-left slanted ray and the left horizontal ray is $50^{\circ}$ (corresponding angles).
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^{\circ}-50^{\circ}-30^{\circ}\\\theta&=100^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.

teachingContext.methodNote: Transfer a corresponding angle and apply the straight-angle sum.
teachingContext.mappingNote: Theta is above the crossing, not the triangle's visibly opposite lower sector.

spec.description: Triangle with its apex on the upper of two horizontal parallel lines, an 85-degree lower-left interior angle and a 150-degree lower-right exterior angle.
spec.mathematics: The lower-right interior angle is 30 degrees; alternate angles transfer 85 and 30 degrees to the apex line, where the three sectors form a straight angle.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 85 and exterior 150 degrees and apex theta only.

answer.short:
$65^{\circ}$

Find the supplementary $30^{\circ}$ angle, transfer both base angles to the upper line, then use a straight angle.
answer.worked:
The lower-right interior angle is $180^{\circ}-150^{\circ}=30^{\circ}$ (angles on a straight line).
The angles beside $\theta$ beneath the upper line are $85^{\circ}$ and $30^{\circ}$ (alternate angles).
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^{\circ}-85^{\circ}-30^{\circ}\\\theta&=65^{\circ}\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.

teachingContext.methodNote: Use a supplementary exterior angle followed by parallel-line transfers and a straight-angle sum.
teachingContext.mappingNote: The compound configuration is solved using the method demonstrated in page 6 Example 1(b), without invoking the triangle-angle-sum theorem.

teachingContext.methodNote: Corresponding and alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles are supplementary. Compound configurations use angle transfers and angles on a straight line.
teachingContext.mappingNote: All ten parts assess unknown angles using the explicitly requested parallel-line approach. Page 6 contains numerical errors in Example 1, so its method is retained while calculations are independently derived.
